passages.text: Then Bildad the Shuhite replied: “How long will you go on saying such things? The words of your mouth are a blustering wind.
passages.sermon:
Bildad was a Shuhite.
Bildad replied to Job.
Bildad spoke directly to Job.
Bildad asked Job a question.
Bildad said, "How long will you keep saying these things?"
Bildad said, "Your words are like a strong, blustering wind."
passages.original: וַ֭יַּעַן בִּלְדַּ֥ד הַשּׁוּחִ֗י וַיֹאמַֽר׃ עַד־ אָ֥ן תְּמַלֶּל־ אֵ֑לֶּה וְר֥וּחַ כַּ֝בִּיר אִמְרֵי־ פִֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Does God pervert justice? Does the Almighty pervert what is right?
passages.sermon:
God is just.
God does not twist justice.
The Almighty is righteous.
The Almighty does not pervert what is right.
passages.original: הַ֭אֵל יְעַוֵּ֣ת מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וְאִם־ שַׁ֝דַּ֗י יְעַוֵּֽת־ צֶֽדֶק׃

passages.text: When your children sinned against Him, He gave them over to their rebellion.
passages.sermon:
Bildad the Shuhite spoke to Job.
Bildad said that Job’s children sinned against God.
God gave Job’s children over to their rebellion.
God allowed them to suffer the consequences of their actions.
passages.original: אִם־ בָּנֶ֥יךָ חָֽטְאוּ־ ל֑וֹ וַֽ֝יְשַׁלְּחֵ֗ם בְּיַד־ פִּשְׁעָֽם׃

passages.text: But if you would earnestly seek God and ask the Almighty for mercy, if you are pure and upright, even now He will rouse Himself on your behalf and restore your righteous estate.
passages.sermon:
God is just and almighty.
You can seek God with all your heart.
You can ask the Almighty for mercy.
If you are pure, God sees your purity.
If you are upright, God knows your honesty.
God will act for you now.
God will restore what is rightfully yours.
God will give back your righteous place.
passages.original: אִם־ אַ֭תָּה תְּשַׁחֵ֣ר אֶל־ אֵ֑ל וְאֶל־ שַׁ֝דַּ֗י תִּתְחַנָּֽן׃ אִם־ זַ֥ךְ וְיָשָׁ֗ר אָ֥תָּה כִּי־ עַ֭תָּה יָעִ֣יר עָלֶ֑יךָ וְ֝שִׁלַּ֗ם נְוַ֣ת צִדְקֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Though your beginnings were modest, your latter days will flourish.
passages.sermon:
Your beginning was small.
Your start was humble.
Your later days will become great.
Your future will prosper greatly.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֣ה רֵאשִׁיתְךָ֣ מִצְעָ֑ר וְ֝אַחֲרִיתְךָ֗ יִשְׂגֶּ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: Please inquire of past generations and consider the discoveries of their fathers.
passages.sermon:
Ask the people who lived before us.
Look at what their fathers discovered.
Learn from the generations that came before you.
Consider the lessons they found.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ שְׁאַל־ נָ֭א לְדֹ֣ר רִישׁ֑וֹן וְ֝כוֹנֵ֗ן לְחֵ֣קֶר אֲבוֹתָֽם׃

passages.text: For we were born yesterday and know nothing; our days on earth are but a shadow.
passages.sermon:
We are people who live now.
We were born only recently.
We do not know much.
Our time on earth is very short.
Our days are like a shadow on the ground.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ תְמ֣וֹל אֲ֭נַחְנוּ וְלֹ֣א נֵדָ֑ע כִּ֤י צֵ֖ל יָמֵ֣ינוּ עֲלֵי־ אָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: Will they not teach you and tell you, and speak from their understanding?
passages.sermon:
The people of past generations have wisdom.
They will teach you.
They will tell you what they know.
They will speak words from their understanding.
They will share what is in their hearts.
passages.original: הֲלֹא־ הֵ֣ם י֭וֹרוּךָ יֹ֣אמְרוּ לָ֑ךְ וּ֝מִלִּבָּ֗ם יוֹצִ֥אוּ מִלִּֽים׃

passages.text: Does papyrus grow where there is no marsh? Do reeds flourish without water?
passages.sermon:
Papyrus is a plant.
Papyrus needs a marsh to grow.
Papyrus cannot grow without a marsh.
Reeds are plants.
Reeds need water to flourish.
Reeds cannot flourish without water.
passages.original: הֲיִֽגְאֶה־ גֹּ֭מֶא בְּלֹ֣א בִצָּ֑ה יִשְׂגֶּה־ אָ֥חוּ בְלִי־ מָֽיִם׃

passages.text: While the shoots are still uncut, they dry up quicker than grass.
passages.sermon:
Papyrus is a plant that grows in marshes.
Its shoots are tender when they first appear.
No one has cut these shoots yet.
These shoots dry up quickly.
They dry up even before the grass dries up.
passages.original: עֹדֶ֣נּוּ בְ֭אִבּוֹ לֹ֣א יִקָּטֵ֑ף וְלִפְנֵ֖י כָל־ חָצִ֣יר יִיבָֽשׁ׃

passages.text: Such is the destiny of all who forget God; so the hope of the godless will perish.
passages.sermon:
This verse describes people who forget God.
These people do not remember God.
They live without God in their thoughts.
Their way of life leads to destruction.
Godless people hope for good things.
Their hope will perish.
Their future will end in disappointment.
passages.original: כֵּ֗ן אָ֭רְחוֹת כָּל־ שֹׁ֣כְחֵי אֵ֑ל וְתִקְוַ֖ת חָנֵ֣ף תֹּאבֵֽד׃

passages.text: His confidence is fragile; his security is in a spider’s web.
passages.sermon:
This man forgets God.
He puts his hope in something weak.
His confidence is fragile.
He trusts in something that cannot last.
His security is like a spider’s web.
A spider’s web is easy to break.
His hope will not stand.
passages.original: אֲשֶׁר־ יָק֥וֹט כִּסְל֑וֹ וּבֵ֥ית עַ֝כָּבִ֗ישׁ מִבְטַחֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He leans on his web, but it gives way; he holds fast, but it does not endure.
passages.sermon:
The godless person trusts in something weak.
He leans on his own house for support.
His house does not stand.
He tries to hold it tightly.
It does not last.
It falls apart.
passages.original: יִשָּׁעֵ֣ן עַל־ בֵּ֭יתוֹ וְלֹ֣א יַעֲמֹ֑ד יַחֲזִ֥יק בּ֝֗וֹ וְלֹ֣א יָקֽוּם׃

passages.text: He is a well-watered plant in the sunshine, spreading its shoots over the garden.
passages.sermon:
This man trusts in himself and not in God.
He is like a plant that receives plenty of water.
The sun shines on him.
He grows quickly.
His shoots spread out over the garden.
passages.original: רָטֹ֣ב ה֭וּא לִפְנֵי־ שָׁ֑מֶשׁ וְעַ֥ל גַּ֝נָּת֗וֹ יֹֽנַקְתּ֥וֹ תֵצֵֽא׃

passages.text: His roots wrap around the rock heap; he looks for a home among the stones.
passages.sermon: A man is like a plant.\r\nHis roots twist around a pile of rocks.\r\nHe searches for a place to live among the stones.
passages.original: עַל־ גַּ֭ל שָֽׁרָשָׁ֣יו יְסֻבָּ֑כוּ בֵּ֖ית אֲבָנִ֣ים יֶחֱזֶֽה׃

passages.text: If he is uprooted from his place, it will disown him, saying, ‘I never saw you.’
passages.sermon:
A plant grows in a certain place.
Someone uproots the plant from its place.
The place rejects the plant.
The place says to the plant, "I never saw you."
passages.original: אִם־ יְבַלְּעֶ֥נּוּ מִמְּקוֹמ֑וֹ וְכִ֥חֶשׁ בּ֝֗וֹ לֹ֣א רְאִיתִֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Surely this is the joy of his way; yet others will spring from the dust.
passages.sermon:
This man finds joy in his own path.
He delights in his way.
But others will grow up from the dust after him.
New people will rise from the ground.
passages.original: הֶן־ ה֭וּא מְשׂ֣וֹשׂ דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וּ֝מֵעָפָ֗ר אַחֵ֥ר יִצְמָֽחוּ׃

passages.text: Behold, God does not reject the blameless, nor will He strengthen the hand of evildoers.
passages.sermon:
God does not reject people who are blameless.
God does not help evildoers.
God does not give strength to those who do wrong.
God supports those who are innocent.
God stands against those who do evil.
passages.original: הֶן־ אֵ֭ל לֹ֣א יִמְאַס־ תָּ֑ם וְלֹֽא־ יַ֝חֲזִ֗יק בְּיַד־ מְרֵעִֽים׃

passages.text: He will yet fill your mouth with laughter, and your lips with a shout of joy.
passages.sermon: God acts with kindness and power.\r\nGod will fill your mouth with laughter.\r\nGod will fill your lips with a shout of joy.
passages.original: עַד־ יְמַלֵּ֣ה שְׂח֣וֹק פִּ֑יךָ וּשְׂפָתֶ֥יךָ תְרוּעָֽה׃

passages.text: Your enemies will be clothed in shame, and the tent of the wicked will be no more.”
passages.sermon:
God will act against your enemies.
Your enemies will feel shame.
God will remove the place where the wicked live.
The tent of the wicked will not remain.
passages.original: שֹׂנְאֶ֥יךָ יִלְבְּשׁוּ־ בֹ֑שֶׁת וְאֹ֖הֶל רְשָׁעִ֣ים אֵינֶֽנּוּ׃פ
